best_for: Paying Proton Mail users who want their mail and calendar in a desktop window instead of a browser tab.

points.title: The app is for paid plans
points.text: Proton says anyone with a paid or trial Proton Mail plan can use the desktop app. On the free plan you get a 14-day trial, then it is back to the web app.

points.title: What paying costs
points.text: Mail Plus is USD 2.49 per month on a 12-month plan (USD 29.88 the first year, then USD 47.88). Proton Unlimited adds Drive, VPN, Pass and Calendar for USD 6.49 per month (USD 77.88 the first year, then USD 119.88). Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Free plan limits
points.text: Proton Free gives one address, 150 messages a day and 500 MB of storage, which grows to 1 GB once you finish a getting-started checklist. Custom domains are not included.

points.title: Mail and calendar in one place
points.text: The app shows Proton Mail and Proton Calendar together, with contacts in a side panel. It has the same features as the web app, and both stay in sync, so you can switch between them.

points.title: Linux is still beta
points.text: Proton calls the Linux app a beta and offers it as DEB, RPM and Snap packages. The Flatpak listed here comes from Flathub, which names Proton AG as developer but does not mark the listing as verified.

points.title: Minimum systems
points.text: Proton lists Windows 10, macOS 12 and Ubuntu 20.04 as the minimums. The Windows installer is x64 only and installs per user. The Windows listing keeps 12 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
